title: Preserve refusal through shopper identity transitions
scope: Preserve existing explicit tracking/personalization refusals through authenticated logout, reset and account linking on both session and object hosts. Resolve only owned stored switches plus restrictive request hints; persist necessary refusal-only replacement state before returning fresh authority, without private profile-cookie restoration. Keep failure recovery restrictive in the shared SDK independently of cleared identity; transfer browser refusal into an existing destination account and make object consent caching commit-aware.
non_goals: No full W05/F05/F10/N06/N11/N12 closure: one aggregate consent policy across capture/events/sort/learning/telemetry/logs/ODP/regional egress, global unknown/absent defaults, historical erasure/retention and customer approval remain open. Automatic refusal transfer does not replace deliberate successful preference updates.

No copied-grant/cross-tab/server-effect revocation, transactional consent/deletion authority or KV consistency redesign; D03/D06 remain human-owned. Continuity cannot survive deliberate clearing/unavailability of all client state across reloads. Do not claim all refused event egress suppressed from a stored-switch test.

No scoring/ranking/model/ledger/new binding/store/harness/framework/broad historical retest programme; no deploy/cloud/credential/customer-data/stage/commit/push/destructive/unrelated changes. Root alone owns tracker, admission and acceptance.

criteria.description: Actual authenticated identity bootstrap/detach/reset and signed account link preserve each false switch independently on both hosts, including cookie-only and stored-only refusal with blocked cookies. Destination true never implicitly upgrades source false. Necessary replacement state contains no prior profile/attributes/affinity/visit advancement; malformed/unreadable source or failed persistence yields no successful new grant or cleared refusal. Preserve tenant/subject/session/backend-proof guards and ordinary consenting success.

Actual shared SDK/router recovery retains restrictive continuity when logout or saved-grant recovery fails, without resurrecting private identity; anonymous bootstrap cannot silently become permissive while continuity is unknown. Recovery hints only restrict; ordinary success and intentional successful preference updates remain distinct. Same-client stale generations remain guarded, scopes do not share recovery flags, and generated SDK bundles match source. DO failed consent persistence cannot publish permissive memory over stored false or suppress a retry.

Independent frozen actual before/current source, fixtures and exact worker evidence review with K1/K2 reruns; inspect app/SDK noEmit, SDK build/syntax/scoped diff and exact relevant artifact identities. Retain baseline and first failures; root separately accepts only this bounded transition containment, without full package/customer/runtime/SLO/release or historical-contract acceptance.
